notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware is attached and no hardware run was made. Only the first card entry symbol is implemented: tactile_gym.rl_envs.exploration.edge_follow.edge_follow_env:EdgeFollowEnv (edge_follow-v0); the card's SurfaceFollowAutoEnv, SurfaceFollowGoalEnv, ObjectRollEnv and ObjectPushEnv are named with file:line in facts.md and are not implemented (one device per package). The fake backend is the package's own pure Python 2-D kinematic stand-in (fake.py) and was never compared with the upstream PyBullet environment; the sim backend (gym.make('edge_follow-v0')) needs PyBullet, OpenCV, numpy and an import of tactile_gym.rl_envs to register the id, and was not run. NOT COVERED: the tactile image, visual image and extended_feature observation arrays; the deployed configuration is observation_mode oracle and the fake serves only the 10-value oracle vector (tcp position, tcp velocity, goal position, edge angle). Five warnings are the expected bridge-derived ones: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed class only sets the seed of the next reset, so it makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived numeric inputs (ticks, seed in reset, seed in seed, action.values). No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings were raised. The risk is R1 because the capability advances a simulated robot arm (simulation stepping, MHS-004 section 2.1); the card's floor is R0 and there is no hardware backend or physical e-stop claim. Only catalogue classes cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
